Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government payments are supported at least for taxes/fees through government platforms: Mali’s DGI states payment of taxes via bank transfer is possible (2018) and Mali launched an online tax payment platform “E-Impôt”/telepayment (2021) for certain taxpayers.
revision_notes: Both original sources verified as live and relevant: the 2018 DGI notice confirms bank-transfer tax payment was made possible, and the December 2021 Ecofin Agency article confirms the e-tax (télépaiement) platform launch, at that time aimed mainly at large and mid-sized companies — consistent with the original 'Limited Use' score. A November 2025 interview with Mali's Director General of Taxes (maliweb.net, corroborated by an identical mali24.info republication) shows the picture has moved on materially: télépaiement is now operational for all taxpayers registered at computerised tax centres, who settle taxes, duties and fees by bank transfer, and electronic tax revenue grew from around 2% of collection in 2022 to roughly 30% (CFA 300 billion) in 2024. This is evidence of active, scaling government uptake rather than a merely capable-but-little-used system, which supports moving the code up to 3 (Yes - Active Use). However télépaiement is currently bank-transfer only (no mobile money or card channel yet, per the DG's own account), and the strong evidence found concerns tax payments specifically — broader P2G charge types named in the variable (licences, fines, utility bills) are not separately confirmed at this level of active use. Because this recalculation reaches the top of the variable's 0-3 scale, it is flagged for human review rather than asserted outright.
revised_comments: Mali's tax authority (Direction Générale des Impôts) operates an e-Impôt/télépaiement platform that lets registered taxpayers at computerised tax centres declare and pay taxes, duties and fees online by bank transfer, following a legal framework adopted in 2019 and the platform's formal launch in December 2021. Uptake has grown substantially: electronic tax revenue rose from around 2% of total tax collection in 2022 to roughly 30% (CFA 300 billion) in 2024. The service currently supports bank transfer only, with mobile money and card payment channels planned but not yet available, and the DGI is working to extend télépaiement to all taxpayer segments and telecommunications networks.
